assumptions: 'Success rate' means attempt-level success rate: successful attempts divided by all attempts, with each retry counted as a separate attempt. Order-level and technical rates are shown alongside.
Period compared: 21-31 October 2026 versus 10-20 October 2026, debit cards only.
caveats: Duplicate records on 12 Oct: 341 attempts were ingested twice (11,704 raw rows vs 11,363 unique attempts, +3.0%). Each attempt is counted once, keeping the first ingestion.
Attempt volume was about 39% above the usual level for those weekdays from 18 Oct to 31 Oct. This is consistent with a sale or a data gap and is flagged for context, not treated as an error.
Success rate depends on the denominator: attempt-level 82.69%, order-level 84.49%, technical 85.09%. Retries and drop-offs explain the gap.
The daily series for Harbor Bank shown covers only up to 21 Oct in the evidence, so the pattern after 21 Oct is inferred from the window-level rate of 74.5%.
Causes are hypotheses: the data shows where and what changed, not why Harbor Bank declined more.

facts.text: Debit card attempt success rate fell 3.32pp, from 86.0% (20,643 of 24,000 attempts) to 82.7% (24,438 of 29,554 attempts). The change is statistically significant.
Only -0.03pp of the change comes from mix (shifts in issuer share); -3.29pp is a like-for-like rate effect within issuers.

Harbor Bank is about 25% of debit volume but accounts for -2.88pp (about 87%) of the -3.32pp change. Its success rate fell 11.33pp, from 85.9% to 74.5%, and its share of attempts barely moved (24.9% to 25.5%).

The other five issuers moved little: Banyan Bank 86.9% to 85.6%, Ridge Bank 86.0% to 85.1%, Coral Bank 85.1% to 84.4%, Indigo Bank 85.8% to 85.6%, Lotus Bank 86.5% to 86.5%. None of these changes were flagged as significant.
For Harbor Bank debit cards, ISSUER_RISK_DECLINE failures rose from 0.45 to 13.96 per 100 attempts (27 to 1,052 failures). No other failure code moved by more than 0.72 per 100 attempts.
Across all debit cards, ISSUER_RISK_DECLINE rose from 0.41 to 3.86 per 100 attempts (98 to 1,142 failures); other codes were roughly flat.
Harbor Bank's daily success rate was between about 84% and 89% through 20 Oct, then dropped to 73.3% on 21 Oct, the first day of the current window.
All four acquirers show a similar drop of about 3pp (Saffron Bank -3.50pp, Northstar Bank -3.49pp, Kestrel Bank -3.43pp, Meridian Bank -2.94pp), so no single acquirer stands out.
The drop is visible under all three definitions in the current window: attempt-level 82.7%, order-level 84.5%, technical 85.1%.

response.headline: Debit card success rate fell 3.32pp, from 86.0% to 82.7%, and almost all of it is a genuine rate decline concentrated at one issuing bank, Harbor Bank, not a mix shift. Harbor Bank's own success rate dropped from 85.9% to 74.5%, and its issuer risk declines jumped sharply.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Ask Harbor Bank whether risk rules or scoring changed on or around 21 Oct; compare declined vs approved attempts on card BIN, amount, channel and merchant category for Harbor Bank.
hypotheses.rationale: The drop is sharp and starts on a single day, is isolated to one issuer across all acquirers, and is almost entirely explained by ISSUER_RISK_DECLINE rising from 0.45 to 13.96 per 100 attempts.
hypotheses.text: Harbor Bank tightened its risk or fraud rules (or changed a risk model/threshold) around 21 Oct, causing many more risk declines on debit cards.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Break Harbor Bank's risk declines down by merchant, channel and ticket size to see whether they are concentrated in particular traffic.
hypotheses.rationale: Volume was elevated from 18 Oct, but Harbor Bank's rate only fell on 21 Oct, and its share of attempts barely changed, so volume alone does not explain it.
hypotheses.text: A specific traffic pattern during the volume spike (e.g. sale-related transactions) triggered Harbor Bank's risk screening.

recommendations.rationale: Harbor Bank explains about 87% of the fall and the failure code points to issuer-side risk declines.
recommendations.text: Contact Harbor Bank's issuer/risk team to confirm any rule or model change from 21 Oct and ask for the decline reason details behind ISSUER_RISK_DECLINE.
